verses.1:1: In various ways and in many manners, God, speaking long ago to the fathers in the prophets,
verses.1:2: has spoken to us last of all in these days in the Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages;
verses.1:3: who, being the splendor of glory and the representation of His substance, and bearing all things by the word of His power, making purification of sins, sits at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
verses.1:4: having become so much better than the angels, by as much as He has inherited a more distinguished name above them.
verses.1:5: For to which of the angels did He ever say, "You are My Son; today I have fathered You"? And again, "I will be a Father to Him, and He will be a Son to Me"?
verses.1:6: And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says, "And let all God's angels worship Him."
verses.1:7: And to the angels indeed He says, "He who makes His angels spirits, and His servants a flame of fire."
verses.1:8: But to the Son, "Your throne, God, is forever and ever; a scepter of equity is the scepter of Your kingdom.
verses.1:9: You loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of exultation above Your companions."
verses.1:10: And, "You, Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the heavens are the works of Your hands.
verses.1:11: They will perish, but You will remain; and they will all grow old like a garment,
verses.1:12: and like a cloak You will change them, and they will be changed; but You are the very same, and Your years will not fail."
verses.1:13: But to which of the angels did He ever say, "Sit at My right hand until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet"?
verses.1:14: Are they not all serving spirits, sent for service on account of those who will obtain the inheritance of salvation?
verses.2:1: Therefore we must all the more heed the things that we have heard, so that we may not perhaps slip away.
verses.2:2: For if the word spoken through angels became firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just repayment of wages,
verses.2:3: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? Having begun to be declared through the Lord, it was confirmed to us by those who heard,
verses.2:4: with God also bearing witness through signs and wonders, and various works of power, and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to His own will.
verses.2:5: For God did not subject to angels the world to come, about which we are speaking.
verses.2:6: But someone has testified in a certain place, saying, "What is man, that You are mindful of him, or a son of man, that You visit him?
verses.2:7: You made him a little less than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor, and You appointed him over the works of Your hands.
verses.2:8: You subjected all things under his feet." For in that He subjected all things to him, He left nothing not subjected to him. But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
verses.2:9: But we see Him who was made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that, by the grace of God, He might taste death for everyone.
verses.2:10: For it was fitting for Him, for whom are all things and through whom are all things, who had brought many sons into glory, to perfect the author of their salvation through suffering.
verses.2:11: For He who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one. For this reason He is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying,
verses.2:12: "I will announce Your name to My brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will praise You."
verses.2:13: And again, "I will be trusting in Him." And again, "Here I am, and My children, whom God has given Me."
verses.2:14: Therefore, since the children have shared in flesh and blood, He Himself likewise partook of the same, so that through death He might destroy the one who held the dominion of death, that is, the devil,
verses.2:15: and might set free those who through fear of death were bound to slavery throughout their whole life.
verses.2:16: For nowhere does He take hold of angels, but He takes hold of the seed of Abraham.
verses.2:17: Therefore He had to be made like the brothers in all things, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest before God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
verses.2:18: For in what He Himself suffered and was tested, He is able also to help those who are being tested.
verses.3:1: Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus,
verses.3:2: who is faithful to Him who made Him, just as Moses also was in all His house.
verses.3:3: For this One has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, by as much as he who built it has greater honor than the house.
verses.3:4: For every house is built by someone, but He who created all things is God.
verses.3:5: And Moses indeed was faithful in His entire house as a servant, for a testimony of the things that were to be spoken;
verses.3:6: but Christ as a Son in His own house, which house we are, if we hold confidence and the glory of hope firm to the end.
verses.3:7: For this reason, just as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear His voice,
verses.3:8: do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, according to the day of testing in the desert,
verses.3:9: where your fathers tested Me, tried Me, and saw My works
verses.3:10: for forty years. Because of this I was angry with this generation and said, 'They always go astray in heart. And they themselves have not known My ways,'
verses.3:11: just as I swore in My wrath, 'They will not enter into My rest.'"
verses.3:12: See to it, brothers, that there does not happen to be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, of departing from the living God;
verses.3:13: but encourage one another every single day, as long as it is called "Today," so that no one of you may be hardened by the deceit of sin.
verses.3:14: For we have become partakers of Christ, if indeed we hold the beginning of His substance firm to the end.
verses.3:15: While it is said, "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as in that provocation."
verses.3:16: For some, on hearing, gave provocation, yet not all who set out from Egypt through Moses.
verses.3:17: And with whom was He angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose corpses fell prostrate in the desert?
verses.3:18: And to whom did He swear that they would not enter into His rest, except to those who were unbelieving?
verses.3:19: And we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.
verses.4:1: Let us fear, therefore, that perhaps, while a promise of entering into His rest remains, anyone among you might be considered to fall short.
verses.4:2: For indeed it was announced to us also, just as to them; yet the word heard did not benefit them, not being mingled with faith from the things that they heard.
verses.4:3: For we who have believed will enter into rest, just as He said, "As I swore in My wrath, 'They will not enter into My rest,'" although indeed the works were completed from the founding of the world.
verses.4:4: For He spoke in a certain place concerning the seventh day in this manner: "And God rested on the seventh day from all His works."
verses.4:5: And in this place again: "They will not enter into My rest."
verses.4:6: Since, therefore, it remains for some to enter into it, and those to whom it was announced first did not enter because of unbelief,
verses.4:7: He again designates a certain day, "Today," saying in David after so long a time, just as was said above: "Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts."
verses.4:8: For if Joshua had granted them rest, He would never speak afterward about another day.
verses.4:9: Consequently, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God.
verses.4:10: For he who has entered into His rest has himself rested from his works as well, just as God did from His own.
verses.4:11: Let us hasten, therefore, to enter into that rest, so that no one may fall into that very same example of unbelief.
verses.4:12: For the word of God is living and effective, more penetrating than any double-edged sword, extending all the way to the division of soul and spirit, as well as of joints and marrow, and a discerner of the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
verses.4:13: And no creature is invisible in His sight, but all things are bare and open to the eyes of Him to whom our account is due.
verses.4:14: Having, therefore, a great high priest who has penetrated the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast the confession.
verses.4:15: For we do not have a high priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tempted in all respects in like manner, without sin.
verses.4:16: Therefore let us approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may obtain mercy and find grace in timely help.
verses.5:1: For every high priest taken from among people is appointed on behalf of people in the things relating to God, so that he may offer gifts and sacrifices for sins,
verses.5:2: who is able to feel compassion for those who are ignorant and go astray, since he himself is also surrounded by weakness;
verses.5:3: and because of this, just as for the people, so also for himself he must make offerings for sins.
verses.5:4: Nor does anyone take the honor for himself, but rather he who is called by God, just as Aaron was.
verses.5:5: In this way Christ also did not glorify Himself to become a high priest, but He who spoke to Him: "You are My Son; today I have fathered You."
verses.5:6: Just as He also says in another place: "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
verses.5:7: In the days of His flesh, offering prayers and supplications with a strong cry and tears to Him who was able to save Him from death, He was heard because of His reverence.
verses.5:8: And indeed, although He was the Son of God, He learned obedience from the things He suffered;
verses.5:9: and having been perfected, He became the cause of eternal salvation to all who obey Him,
verses.5:10: designated by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.5:11: Concerning this we have a great discourse, and one that cannot be explained in words, because you have become weak in hearing.
verses.5:12: For indeed, although you ought to be teachers because of the time, you again need to be taught what the basic elements of the beginning of the words of God are, and you have become those who need milk, not solid food.
verses.5:13: For everyone who partakes of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a small child.
verses.5:14: Solid food, however, belongs to the mature, to those who through habit have their senses trained for the discernment of good and evil.
verses.6:1: For this reason, setting aside the introductory word about Christ, let us be carried forward to more mature things, not again laying a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
verses.6:2: of teaching concerning baptisms, also of the laying on of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
verses.6:3: And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
verses.6:4: For it is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, have also tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
verses.6:5: and have likewise tasted the good word of God and the powers of the coming age,
verses.6:6: and have fallen away, to be renewed again to repentance, crucifying again for themselves the Son of God and holding Him up to public spectacle.
verses.6:7: For ground that drinks in the rain often coming upon it, and produces vegetation suitable for those by whom it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God;
verses.6:8: but when it brings forth thorns and thistles, it is rejected and close to a curse, whose end is burning.
verses.6:9: Yet concerning you, dearly beloved, we are confident of better things, and things nearer to salvation, even though we speak in this way.
verses.6:10: For God is not unjust, that He would forget your work and the love you have shown in His name, you who have served the saints and continue to serve them.
verses.6:11: And we desire each one of you to display the same diligence toward the fulfillment of hope all the way to the end,
verses.6:12: so that you may not become sluggish, but rather imitators of those who through faith and patience will inherit the promises.
verses.6:13: For God, in making a promise to Abraham, because He had no one greater by whom He might swear, swore by Himself,
verses.6:14: saying, "Surely, blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you."
verses.6:15: And in this way, enduring patiently, he attained the promise.
verses.6:16: For people swear by someone greater than themselves, and an oath, for confirmation, is the end of every dispute among them.
verses.6:17: In this matter, God, wishing more abundantly to show to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of His counsel, interposed an oath,
verses.6:18: so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have the strongest consolation, we who have fled for refuge to lay hold of the hope set before us,
verses.6:19: which we have as an anchor of the soul, secure and firm, and entering all the way into the interior behind the veil,
verses.6:20: where Jesus entered on our behalf as a forerunner, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.7:1: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of the Most High God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
verses.7:2: to whom Abraham also apportioned tithes of everything, being translated first indeed as king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace,
verses.7:3: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, yet likened to the Son of God, remains a priest perpetually.
verses.7:4: Now consider how great this man is, to whom Abraham the patriarch even gave tithes from the choicest things.
verses.7:5: And indeed, those from the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, from their own brothers, although they themselves also came out from the loins of Abraham.
verses.7:6: But the one whose lineage is not counted among them took tithes from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.
verses.7:7: Now without any dispute, what is lesser is blessed by the superior.
verses.7:8: And here indeed, men who die receive tithes; but there it is testified that he lives.
verses.7:9: And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, who received tithes, was tithed;
verses.7:10: for he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.
verses.7:11: If therefore perfection was through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law), what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be named according to the order of Aaron?
verses.7:12: For with the priesthood changed, it is necessary that a change of the law also take place.
verses.7:13: For He concerning whom these things are spoken belongs to another tribe, from which no one has served at the altar.
verses.7:14: For it is evident that our Lord arose from Judah, regarding which tribe Moses spoke nothing about priests.
verses.7:15: And it is still more evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
verses.7:16: who has become so not according to the law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indissoluble life.
verses.7:17: For it is testified, "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
verses.7:18: Indeed, a setting aside of the preceding commandment takes place because of its weakness and uselessness;
verses.7:19: for the law brought nothing to perfection; on the other hand, there is the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
verses.7:20: And to the extent that this is not without an oath (indeed, others were made priests without an oath,
verses.7:21: but He with an oath through the One who said to Him, "The Lord has sworn, and He will not repent: You are a priest forever"),
verses.7:22: to that same extent Jesus has become the guarantor of a better covenant.
verses.7:23: And indeed, those others were made priests in greater numbers, for the reason that they were prevented by death from continuing;
verses.7:24: but He, because He remains forever, holds an everlasting priesthood.
verses.7:25: Consequently, He is also able to save perpetually those who approach God through Himself, always living to intercede for us.
verses.7:26: For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
verses.7:27: who does not have a daily necessity, like the priests, to offer sacrifices first for His own offenses, and then for those of the people; for this He did once, by offering Himself.
verses.7:28: For the law appoints men as priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which is after the law, appoints the Son, perfected forever.
verses.8:1: Now the main point regarding the things being said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of Majesty in the heavens,
verses.8:2: a minister of the holy places and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
verses.8:3: For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary that this One also have something to offer.
verses.8:4: If therefore He were on earth, He would not even be a priest, since there are those who offer gifts according to the law,
verses.8:5: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things. Just as an answer was given to Moses when he was completing the tabernacle: "See," He says, "make all things according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain."
verses.8:6: But now He has obtained a better ministry, by as much as He is also the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted upon better promises.
verses.8:7: For if that first one had been free of fault, surely no place would be sought for a second.
verses.8:8: For finding fault with them, He says, "Look, days will come, says the Lord, and I will accomplish a new covenant over the house of Israel and over the house of Judah,
verses.8:9: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they themselves did not continue in My covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
verses.8:10: For this is the covenant that I will establish for the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: giving My laws into their mind, and upon their heart I will inscribe them; and I will be God to them, and they themselves will be a people to Me;
verses.8:11: and each one will not teach his neighbor, and each one his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' because all will know Me, from the least to the greatest of them;
verses.8:12: for I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and their sins I will remember no longer."
verses.8:13: Now in saying "new," He has made the first obsolete. And what is becoming antiquated and growing old is close to perishing.
verses.9:1: Now indeed, the first one also had ordinances of worship and an earthly sanctuary.
verses.9:2: For a first tabernacle was made, in which were the lampstands, and the table, and the presentation of the loaves, which is called the Holy Place.
verses.9:3: And behind the second veil was the tabernacle that is called the Holy of Holies,
verses.9:4: having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant covered on every side with gold, in which was a golden jar holding the manna, and the rod of Aaron that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant,
verses.9:5: and above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat; concerning which we are not now to speak in detail.
verses.9:6: Now with these things arranged in this way, the priests continually entered into the first tabernacle, performing the duties of the sacrifices;
verses.9:7: but into the second, once a year, the high priest alone, not without blood, which he offers for his own ignorance and that of the people;
verses.9:8: the Holy Spirit signifying this, that the way into the holy places had not yet been disclosed while the first tabernacle still had standing,
verses.9:9: which is a parable of the present time, according to which gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot make the one who serves perfect with respect to conscience, only in foods and in drinks,
verses.9:10: and various washings, and ordinances of the flesh imposed until the time of reformation.
verses.9:11: But Christ, being present as a high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made by hands, that is, not of this creation,
verses.9:12: and not through the blood of goats or calves, but through His own blood, entered once into the holy places, having obtained eternal redemption.
verses.9:13: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkled ashes of a heifer, sanctify those who are defiled for the cleansing of the flesh,
verses.9:14: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
verses.9:15: And for this reason He is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, with a death intervening for the redemption of those transgressions that were under the first covenant, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
verses.9:16: For where there is a testament, it is necessary that the death of the testator intervene.
verses.9:17: For a testament is confirmed in the case of the dead; otherwise it is not yet valid while the one who made the testament lives.
verses.9:18: Consequently, not even the first one was dedicated without blood.
verses.9:19: For when every commandment of the law had been read by Moses to all the people, taking the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
verses.9:20: saying, "This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded for you."
verses.9:21: Moreover, he likewise sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry.
verses.9:22: And almost all things are cleansed in blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
verses.9:23: Therefore it is necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
verses.9:24: For Jesus did not enter into holy places made by hands, copies of the true ones, but into heaven itself, so that He may now appear before the face of God for us;
verses.9:25: nor that He should offer Himself often, just as the high priest enters into the holy places year by year with blood not his own;
verses.9:26: otherwise He would have had to suffer repeatedly from the beginning of the world; but now, once at the consummation of the ages, He has appeared for the abolition of sin through His sacrifice.
verses.9:27: And just as it is appointed for human beings to die once, and after this comes judgment,
verses.9:28: so Christ also was offered once to drain away the sins of many; a second time He will appear without sin to those who await Him, for salvation.
verses.10:1: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the things, can never, with those very same sacrifices that they offer unceasingly year by year, make those who approach perfect;
verses.10:2: otherwise they would have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, having been cleansed once, would no longer have any consciousness of sin;
verses.10:3: but in them a remembrance of sins is made year by year.
verses.10:4: For it is impossible for sins to be taken away by the blood of bulls and goats.
verses.10:5: Therefore, entering the world, He says, "Sacrifice and offering You did not want, but a body You prepared for Me;
verses.10:6: burnt offerings for sin did not please You.
verses.10:7: Then I said, 'Look, I come (at the head of the book it is written about Me) to do Your will, God.'"
verses.10:8: Saying above, "Sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings for sin You did not want, nor were they pleasing to You" (which are offered according to the law),
verses.10:9: "Then I said, 'Look, I come to do Your will, God,'" He takes away the first so that He may establish what follows.
verses.10:10: In this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once.
verses.10:11: And every priest indeed stands ready daily, ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins;
verses.10:12: but this One, offering one sacrifice for sins, sits forever at the right hand of God,
verses.10:13: waiting from then on until His enemies are placed as a footstool for His feet.
verses.10:14: For by one offering He has perfected forever those who have been sanctified.
verses.10:15: Moreover, the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us; for after He said,
verses.10:16: "Now this is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord, by giving My laws in their hearts, and on their minds I will inscribe them,
verses.10:17: and their sins and their iniquities I will not remember anymore."
verses.10:18: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.
verses.10:19: Therefore, brothers, having confidence in the entrance to the holy places by the blood of Christ,
verses.10:20: which He initiated for us as a new and living way through the veil, that is, His flesh,
verses.10:21: and a great priest over the house of God,
verses.10:22: let us approach with a true heart in fullness of faith, with our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our body washed with clean water;
verses.10:23: let us hold the confession of our hope unswerving (for He is faithful who promised),
verses.10:24: and let us consider one another for the stirring up of love and good works,
verses.10:25: not deserting our gathering, as is the custom of some, but offering encouragement, and all the more as you see the day approaching.
verses.10:26: For if we sin willfully after having received the knowledge of the truth, there is no longer left a sacrifice for sins,
verses.10:27: but a certain terrifying expectation of judgment, and a zeal of fire that is about to consume the adversaries.
verses.10:28: Anyone who makes the law of Moses void dies without any compassion by two or three witnesses;
verses.10:29: how much more do you suppose that one deserves worse punishments, who has trampled on the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant in which he was sanctified as defiled, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
verses.10:30: For we know the One who said, "To Me belongs vengeance, and I will repay." And again, "The Lord will judge His people."
verses.10:31: It is dreadful to fall into the hands of the living God.
verses.10:32: But remember the earlier days, in which, having been enlightened, you endured a great struggle of sufferings,
verses.10:33: both on the one hand made a spectacle by reproaches and tribulations, and on the other hand becoming companions of those living in such a way.
verses.10:34: For you both sympathized with those in chains and accepted with joy the plundering of your goods, knowing that you have a better and enduring possession.
verses.10:35: Therefore, do not lose your confidence, which has a great reward.
verses.10:36: For endurance is necessary for you, so that, doing the will of God, you may obtain the promise.
verses.10:37: For, "Yet a very little while, He who is to come will come and will not delay;
verses.10:38: and My righteous one lives by faith; yet if he withdraws himself, he will not please My soul."
verses.10:39: But we are not sons of withdrawal to destruction, but of faith to the gaining of the soul.
verses.11:1: Now faith is the substance of things to be hoped for, the proof of things that do not appear.
verses.11:2: For in this the elders obtained testimony.
verses.11:3: By faith we understand that the ages were fashioned by the word of God, so that from invisible things visible things might come into being.
verses.11:4: By faith Abel offered to God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he obtained testimony that he was righteous, with God bearing testimony to his gifts; and through it, though dead, he still speaks.
verses.11:5: By faith Enoch was taken away so that he would not see death, and he was not found, because God took him away; for before his removal he had testimony that he had pleased God.
verses.11:6: Now without faith it is impossible to please God. For the one who approaches God must believe that He exists, and that He is a rewarder to those who seek Him.
verses.11:7: By faith Noah, having received a response concerning the things that were not yet seen, in fear fashioned an ark for the saving of his household, through which he condemned the world and was appointed heir of the righteousness that is through faith.
verses.11:8: By faith the one who is called Abraham obeyed to depart for a place that he was about to receive as an inheritance; and he departed, not knowing where he was going.
verses.11:9: By faith he resided in the land of promise as in a foreign land, living in small huts with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.
verses.11:10: For he was waiting for the city that has foundations, whose architect and founder is God.
verses.11:11: By faith Sarah herself also, though barren, received power for the conception of seed even past the time of life, since she believed that He who had promised was faithful.
verses.11:12: For this reason also, there sprang from one man (and him already lifeless) as many as the stars of heaven in multitude, and like the sand that is by the shore of the sea, innumerable.
verses.11:13: All these died according to faith, not having received the promises, but seeing them from afar and greeting them, and confessing that they are foreigners and guests on the earth.
verses.11:14: For those who say these things indicate that they are seeking a homeland.
verses.11:15: And indeed, if they had remembered that one from which they went out, they would certainly have had time to return.
verses.11:16: But now they long for a better one, that is, a heavenly one. For this reason God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He prepared a city for them.
verses.11:17: By faith Abraham offered Isaac when he was tested, and the one who had received the promises was offering his only-begotten son,
verses.11:18: to whom it was said, "In Isaac your seed will be named,"
verses.11:19: considering that God is able to raise up even from the dead, from which he also received him as a parable.
verses.11:20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau even concerning things to come.
verses.11:21: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshiped the top of his staff.
verses.11:22: By faith Joseph, as he was dying, made mention of the departure of the sons of Israel and gave instructions concerning his bones.
verses.11:23: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the infant was handsome, and they did not fear the king's edict.
verses.11:24: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, denied that he was the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
verses.11:25: choosing rather to be afflicted with the people of God than to have the delight of temporary sin,
verses.11:26: esteeming the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasure of the Egyptians, for he was looking toward the reward.
verses.11:27: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the fury of the king, for he endured as though seeing the Invisible One.
verses.11:28: By faith he celebrated the Passover and the pouring out of blood, so that the one who was destroying the firstborn would not touch them.
verses.11:29: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as through dry land; when the Egyptians attempted this, they were swallowed up.
verses.11:30: By faith the walls of Jericho collapsed after seven days of circling.
verses.11:31: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with the unbelievers, welcoming the spies in peace.
verses.11:32: And what more should I say? For time will fail me as I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,
verses.11:33: who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, attained promises, closed the mouths of lions,
verses.11:34: extinguished the force of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, recovered strength from weakness, became mighty in war, routed the armies of foreigners.
verses.11:35: Women received their dead from resurrection; but others were stretched on the rack, not accepting release, so that they might find a better resurrection.
verses.11:36: Still others experienced mockings and whippings, and furthermore chains and prisons.
verses.11:37: They were stoned, they were sawn apart, they were tested, they died by the slaughter of the sword; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, destitute, hard-pressed, afflicted,
verses.11:38: of whom the world was not worthy, wandering in deserts, in mountains, in caves, and in caverns of the earth.
verses.11:39: And all these, approved by the testimony of faith, did not receive the promise,
verses.11:40: with God providing something better for us, so that they would not be brought to completion without us.
verses.12:1: Therefore we also, having so great a cloud of witnesses set over us, laying aside every weight and the sin that surrounds us, let us run through endurance to the contest set before us,
verses.12:2: looking to the author and completer of faith, Jesus, who, having joy set before Him, endured the cross, despising the shame, and sits at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.12:3: For reflect carefully on Him who endured such opposition from sinners against Himself, so that you may not grow weary, failing in your minds.
verses.12:4: For you have not yet resisted to the point of blood, fighting against sin,
verses.12:5: and you have forgotten the consolation that speaks to you as to sons, saying, "My son, do not neglect the discipline of the Lord, nor grow weary while you are reproved by Him.
verses.12:6: For the one whom the Lord loves, He chastises, and He scourges every son whom He receives."
verses.12:7: Persevere in discipline. God offers Himself to you as to sons; for what son is there whom a father does not correct?
verses.12:8: But if you are outside discipline, of which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate, and not sons.
verses.12:9: Furthermore, we indeed had the fathers of our flesh as instructors, and we revered them; will we not much more obey the Father of spirits and live?
verses.12:10: And they indeed, for a time of a few days, instructed us according to their own will, but He for what is beneficial, in receiving His sanctification.
verses.12:11: Now all discipline for the present indeed seems not to be of joy, but of sorrow; afterward, however, it will yield the most peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.
verses.12:12: For this reason, lift up the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
verses.12:13: and make straight steps for your feet, so that no one who limps may go astray, but rather be healed.
verses.12:14: Follow peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see God,
verses.12:15: watching closely so that no one falls short of the grace of God, so that no root of bitterness sprouting upward may hinder, and through it many be defiled;
verses.12:16: so that no one be a fornicator or a profane person like Esau, who for a single meal sold his firstborn rights.
verses.12:17: For know that afterward also, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place of repentance, although he had sought it with tears.
verses.12:18: For you have not approached a mountain that can be touched, and a blazing fire, and a whirlwind, and darkness, and a storm,
verses.12:19: and the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; those who heard it excused themselves, so that no word would be spoken to them.
verses.12:20: For they could not bear what was being said: "Even if a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned."
verses.12:21: And what was seen was so terrifying; Moses said, "I am terrified and trembling."
verses.12:22: But you have approached Mount Zion, and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and the throng of many thousands of angels,
verses.12:23: and the church of the firstborn, who are enrolled in the heavens, and God, the Judge of all, and the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
verses.12:24: and Jesus, the mediator of the new covenant, and the sprinkling of blood, speaking better than Abel.
verses.12:25: See that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if they did not escape when they refused Him who was speaking on earth, much more will we not escape, who turn away from Him who speaks to us from the heavens.
verses.12:26: His voice shook the earth then, but now He promises, saying, "Yet once more, and I will shake not only the earth, but also heaven."
verses.12:27: Now His saying, "Yet once more," declares the removal of movable things, as of things that have been made, so that the things that are immovable may remain.
verses.12:28: Therefore, receiving an immovable kingdom, we have grace, through which let us serve, pleasing God with fear and reverence.
verses.12:29: For indeed our God is a consuming fire.
verses.13:1: Let brotherly love remain in you,
verses.13:2: and do not forget hospitality; for through this some unknowingly received angels as guests.
verses.13:3: Remember those who are bound, as though bound together with them, and those who suffer hardship, as you yourselves also dwell in the body.
verses.13:4: Let marriage be honorable among all, and the marriage bed unstained. For God will judge fornicators and adulterers.
verses.13:5: Let your way of life be without greed, content with what is at hand; for He Himself has said, "I will not desert you, nor will I abandon you,"
verses.13:6: so that we say with confidence, "The Lord is a helper to me; I will not fear what man may do to me."
verses.13:7: Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you; looking closely at the outcome of their conduct, imitate their faith.
verses.13:8: Jesus Christ, yesterday and today, is the same also forever.
verses.13:9: Do not be drawn away by various and foreign teachings. For it is best to establish the heart by grace, not by foods, which have not benefited those walking in them.
verses.13:10: We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle do not have authority to eat.
verses.13:11: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought for sin into the holy places through the high priest are burned outside the camp.
verses.13:12: For this reason Jesus also suffered outside the gate, so that He might sanctify the people through His own blood.
verses.13:13: Let us therefore go out to Him outside the camp, carrying His reproach.
verses.13:14: For we do not have an enduring city here, but we seek out the one to come.
verses.13:15: Through Him therefore let us always offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips confessing His name.
verses.13:16: And do not forget beneficence and sharing; for by such sacrifices God's favor is won.
verses.13:17: Obey your leaders and be subject to them. For they themselves keep watch as those who will render an account for your souls, so that they may do this with joy and not groaning; for this is not beneficial for you.
verses.13:18: Pray for us, for we are confident that we have a good conscience, wishing to conduct ourselves well in all things.
verses.13:19: And I implore you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you more quickly.
verses.13:20: Now may the God of peace, who brought out from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep, in the blood of the eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.13:21: equip you in every good thing, so that you may do His will, working in you what is pleasing before Him through Jesus Christ, to whom belongs glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.13:22: Now I ask you, brothers, that you bear with the word of consolation. For indeed I have written to you in very few words.
verses.13:23: Know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom, if he comes soon, I will see you.
verses.13:24: Greet all your leaders, and all the saints. The brothers from Italy greet you.
verses.13:25: May grace be with all of you. Amen.

notes.1:3: The Vulgate uses the present tense "sedet" ("sits") rather than the Greek aorist ("sat down"), and renders Greek "charakter tes hypostaseos autou" as "figura substantiae ejus" ("the representation of His substance").
notes.1:7: Latin "spiritus" (rendering Greek "pneumata") can mean either "spirits" or "winds"; translating "spirits" preserves the direct verbal link with "serving spirits" ("spiritus") in 1:14.
notes.1:8: The Vulgate reads "regni tui" ("of Your kingdom"), whereas some modern critical Greek editions read "of his kingdom."
notes.1:12: The Vulgate reads "mutabis eos" ("You will change them," matching Greek witnesses with "allaxeis"), whereas most modern critical Greek editions read "roll them up" ("helixeis").
notes.2:5: The Vulgate explicitly supplies "Deus" ("God") as the subject of "subjecit," whereas the Greek leaves the subject unexpressed.
notes.2:7: The Vulgate includes the third clause from Psalm 8:7, "et constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum" ("and You appointed him over the works of Your hands"), which is omitted in many modern critical Greek editions.
notes.2:10: The Vulgate uses the pluperfect relative clause "qui ... adduxerat" ("who had brought") and singular "per passionem" ("through suffering"), where the Greek is plural.
notes.2:16: The Vulgate renders Greek "ou depou" ("surely not") as "Nusquam" ("nowhere"); "apprehendit" means "takes hold of."
notes.3:6: The Vulgate reads "in domo sua" ("in His own house," where the Greek has "over"), nominative "quae domus" ("which house," where most Greek texts have "whose house"), and "gloriam spei" ("the glory of hope," where the Greek has "boasting/pride of hope").
notes.3:11: Latin literally reads "Si introibunt in requiem meam" ("If they will enter into My rest"), reproducing the Hebrew elliptical oath formula for an emphatic negative (cf. 3:18).
notes.3:14: The Vulgate adds "ejus" in "initium substantiae ejus" ("the beginning of His substance," matching "substantiae ejus" in 1:3), whereas the Greek lacks "his."
notes.3:16: The Vulgate reads declarative statements ("Quidam ... sed non universi," "For some ... yet not all"), whereas modern critical Greek editions punctuate the verse as two rhetorical questions ("Who ...? Was it not all ...?").
notes.3:18: The Vulgate reads "increduli fuerunt" ("were unbelieving"), tying the verse lexically to "incredulitatis" and "incredulitatem" ("unbelief") in 3:12 and 3:19, whereas the Greek uses a term meaning "disobedient."
notes.4:2: The Vulgate reads non admistus fidei ex iis quae audierunt ("not mingled with faith from the things that they heard"), taking the participle with sermo ("word") and using the neuter quae ("the things which") rather than the Greek masculine referring to "those who heard."
notes.4:3: The Vulgate uses the future tense Ingrediemur ("will enter") where Greek has a present tense. Both here and in 4:5, Latin Si introibunt literally means "If they will enter," preserving a Semitic elliptical oath idiom expressing emphatic negation ("They will not enter").
notes.4:6: Both here and in 4:11, the Vulgate reads incredulitatem ("unbelief"), rendering Greek apeitheia ("disobedience") specifically as lack of faith.
notes.4:8: The Latin literally reads Jesus, the Greco-Latin form of the Hebrew name Joshua, referring here to Joshua son of Nun who led Israel into Canaan.
notes.4:13: Latin ad quem nobis sermo literally means "to whom our word [is]," a concise idiom signifying either "to whom our account is due" or "of whom we are speaking."
notes.5:2: The Vulgate uses condolere ("to feel compassion for," literally "to suffer along with") to translate Greek metriopathein ("to deal gently with").
notes.5:8: The Vulgate explicitly reads Filius Dei ("the Son of God"), whereas the Greek text reads simply "a Son."
notes.5:11: Latin De quo may refer either to the subject matter ("Concerning this") or to Melchizedek ("Concerning him"). The Vulgate also renders Greek dysermeneutos ("hard to explain") with ininterpretabilis and nothroi ("dull") with imbecilles ("weak").
notes.5:12: The Vulgate uses the passive ut vos doceamini ("that you be taught"), compared with the Greek active construction ("that someone teach you").
notes.6:1: The Vulgate uses the neuter plural comparative ad perfectiora ("to more mature things," literally "to more perfect things"), whereas the Greek reads the singular abstract noun teleioteta ("maturity/perfection").
notes.6:6: The Vulgate uses the passive infinitive renovari ("to be renewed") rather than the Greek active ("to renew"), and adds the explicit adverb rursum ("again") with crucifigentes.
notes.6:7: The Vulgate reads the agent phrase a quibus colitur ("by whom it is cultivated"), where the Greek reads di' hous ("for whose sake").
notes.6:12: The Vulgate uses the future tense haereditabunt ("will inherit"), where the Greek has a present participle ("who are inheriting"); in 6:11 the Vulgate also reads expletionem ("fulfillment") for Greek plerophorian ("full assurance").
notes.6:14: The Latin quotation literally opens with Nisi ("Unless / If not"), reflecting the Semitic positive oath formula (matching Greek ei men / e men) used to express emphatic certainty ("Surely").
notes.7:4: Latin "de praecipuis" literally means "from the choicest things" (or "principal things"), rendering Greek "akrothinion" ("choicest spoils") without explicitly specifying spoils.
notes.7:24: The Vulgate renders Greek "aparabaton" ("permanent" or "non-transferable") temporally as "sempiternum" ("everlasting").
notes.7:25: The Vulgate translates Greek "eis to panteles" ("completely" or "for all time") temporally as "in perpetuum" ("perpetually") and reads "pro nobis" ("for us") where most Greek manuscripts have "for them."
notes.7:27: Both here and in 7:28, the Vulgate uses "sacerdotes" ("priests") rather than "pontifices" ("high priests"), whereas the Greek text has "archiereis" ("high priests").
notes.8:5: The Vulgate uses the same noun "exemplar" both for the earthly copy (Greek "hypodeigma") and for the heavenly pattern shown to Moses (Greek "typos"), and "responsum est" ("an answer was given") renders Greek "kechrematistai" ("was divinely instructed").
notes.8:8: The Vulgate uses the future tense "venient" ("will come"), whereas the Greek text has the present "erchontai" ("are coming").
notes.8:11: The Vulgate reads "proximum" ("neighbor"), aligning with a Septuagint and Greek manuscript variant, where the critical Greek text has "politen" ("fellow citizen").
notes.9:2: The Vulgate reads plural "candelabra" ("lampstands"), whereas the Greek text has singular "lychnia" ("lampstand").
notes.9:14: The Vulgate reads "per Spiritum Sanctum" ("through the Holy Spirit"), whereas most Greek manuscripts read "through an eternal Spirit."
notes.9:16: Latin "testamentum" (like Greek "diatheke") carries both the sense of "covenant" and "last will/testament," underpinning the legal argument about a testator's death across 9:15-18.
notes.9:19: The Vulgate has "lecto" ("read") and "mandato legis" ("commandment of the law"), whereas the Greek text reads "spoken" and "according to the law."
notes.9:24: The Vulgate reads "Jesus," whereas the Greek text reads "Christos" ("Christ").
notes.9:28: The Vulgate translates Greek "anenenkein" ("to bear") with "exhaurienda" ("to drain away" or "to exhaust").
notes.10:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads this clause as a declarative statement (alioquin cessassent offerri, without a negative) rather than the rhetorical question found in most Greek manuscripts ("would they not have ceased to be offered?").
notes.10:6: Latin holocautomata pro peccato ("burnt offerings for sin," also in v. 8) omits the conjunction "and" present in the Greek ("burnt offerings and [offerings] for sin").
notes.10:9: The Clementine Vulgate has first-person tunc dixi ("Then I said"), quoting the introductory words from v. 7 directly, whereas the Greek has third-person "then he has said"; Latin sequens also literally means "what follows" rather than Greek "the second."
notes.10:19: The Clementine Vulgate reads in sanguine Christi ("by the blood of Christ"), whereas the Greek text has "by the blood of Jesus."
notes.10:39: Latin subtractionis filii ("sons of withdrawal") includes filii ("sons"), a Vulgate-distinct addition not present in the Greek text.
notes.11:1: Latin sperandarum substantia rerum, argumentum non apparentium uses the gerundive sperandarum ("things to be hoped for"), substantia ("substance"), and argumentum ("proof"), rendering Greek hypostasis and elenchos.
notes.11:3: The Vulgate states the clause positively as ut ex invisibilibus visibilia fierent ("so that from invisible things visible things might come into being"), whereas the Greek states negatively that what is seen was not made out of things that appear.
notes.11:8: The Vulgate reads qui vocatur Abraham ("the one who is called Abraham") rather than "Abraham, when he was called."
notes.11:21: The Vulgate takes fastigium virgae ejus as the direct object of adoravit ("worshiped the top of his staff"), omitting the Greek preposition epi ("upon" or "leaning upon").
notes.11:28: The Vulgate reads sanguinis effusionem ("pouring out of blood") rather than "sprinkling of blood" (Greek proschysin), contrasting with sanguinis aspersionem ("sprinkling of blood") in 12:24.
notes.12:1: The Vulgate reads impositam ("set over us") rather than "surrounding us" and circumstans nos peccatum ("the sin that surrounds us") rather than "sin that so easily entangles."
notes.12:7: The Vulgate renders In disciplina perseverate as a direct imperative ("Persevere in discipline") and translates Greek prospheretai ("deals with you") literally as offert se ("offers Himself").
notes.12:8: Latin adulteri is used here in the sense of spurious or illegitimate offspring, rendering Greek nothoi ("illegitimate children").
notes.12:14: The Vulgate reads Deum ("God") where the Greek text reads ton kyrion ("the Lord").
notes.12:28: The Vulgate reads the indicative habemus gratiam ("we have grace") rather than the Greek hortatory subjunctive echomen charin ("let us be thankful"), making "grace" the means by which believers serve God in the following clause.
notes.13:2: The Vulgate reads latuerunt quidam, angelis hospitio receptis (literally "some were hidden/unaware, angels having been received as guests"), a literal Latin calque of the Greek idiom for entertaining angels unknowingly.
notes.13:6: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive faciat (non timebo quid faciat mihi homo) to form an indirect question ("I will not fear what man may do to me"), rather than splitting the quotation into a separate direct question ("What can man do to me?").
notes.13:9: The Clementine Vulgate uses the superlative Optimum ("best") and the active infinitive stabilire cor ("to establish the heart"), whereas the Greek has the positive adjective ("good") with a passive infinitive ("for the heart to be strengthened").
notes.13:16: The Vulgate renders the Greek verb for being well pleased with the passive promeretur Deus ("God's favor is won" or "God is won over"), reflecting ecclesiastical Latin usage of promereri for gaining divine favor.
notes.13:21: The Clementine Vulgate reads in omni bono ("in every good thing," without "work"), in vobis ("in you," rather than "in us"), and the explicit indicative cui est gloria ("to whom belongs glory").
